description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

summary.one_liner: Bazel is a build and test system for software of any size, aiming to be fast and correct across multiple languages and platforms.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Bazel as a build tool that rebuilds only what has changed, using local and distributed caching, dependency analysis and parallel execution for incremental builds. It states support for building and testing Java, C++, Android, iOS, Go and other language platforms. It says Bazel runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. It is positioned for codebases in multiple repositories or a large monorepo. Extensibility comes through Bazel's extension language, which lets users add new languages and share rules with the community. The README itself is short and mainly links to external docs for installation, tutorials, the command line, rule reference and extension guides.
use_cases: building Java, C++, Go, Android or iOS projects in one tool
adding support for a new language or platform via custom rules
how_to_run: Install Bazel (see the install guide linked from the README)
Follow the Getting Started tutorials (Build C++, Build Java, Android, iOS)
Consult the Bazel command line and rule reference documentation
notable: Rebuilds only what is necessary, with local and distributed caching
Multi-language support including Java, C++, Android, iOS and Go
Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux
Extensible through a familiar extension language and shareable language rules
caveats: The README does not list installation steps inline; setup is delegated to external docs
Platform-specific rule support beyond the named languages is not detailed in the README
